subject: SCCs: decision matrix + local law considerations for Acme Health
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Priya Menon <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SCCs: decision matrix + local law considerations for Acme Health

Hi Priya + team,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a decision matrix we put together that maps the recommended SCC module(s) to the different data flows you described (PHI-adjacent analytics, de-identified telemetry, and support logs). The spreadsheet also includes a short local-law risk note for the UK and a separate column for operational impacts (latency/cost) if we fall back to a different model variant in-region.

High level:
- For customer-supplied PHI where Acme is controller and Redwood acts solely as processor, Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is our baseline recommendation for EU transfers.
- For cross-border routing to our US-hosted analytics cluster (where Acme also controls the analytics bucket), the matrix highlights two options: Module 2 + UK Addendum (preferred) or Module 1 with demonstrable supplementary controls if you need a processor-to-processor path.

Two specific asks:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme must preserve the right to audit logs for inpatient data (this affects Module/Annex choices)?
2) Any local-law flags from your UK counsel on the Addendum language we included in the draft?

I've copied Karthik and Laura for ops/implementation input — please see the matrix tab labelled "Ops Impact".

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sccs-decision-matrix.xlsx, uk-addendum-draft.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dr. Priya Menon <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SCCs: decision matrix + local law considerations for Acme Health

Aisha / Priya — quick ops read-through:

Thanks for drafting this — a few operational notes that feed into the selection matrix: 
- If we go Module 2 with the UK Addendum, we can keep most inference workloads in our multi-tenant EU region and avoid runtime fallbacks. Cost delta: ~4-7% due to additional logging and KMS calls.
- If Acme requires a processor-to-processor contractual model (Module 1 route), we'll need to instantiate a dedicated ingest pipeline and separate key material per account (adds ~2 weeks to rollout, higher sustained cost).
- For PHI-adjacent analytics where we only receive de-identified aggregates, a narrow-scoped Module 2 + documented pseudonymization controls should be sufficient. Note: we should capture the pseudonymization proof in the DPIA for audit.

Proposed recommendation (ops): Module 2 + UK Addendum for EU/UK routing; include a fall-back item in the contract for Module 1 pathway if regulators require additional isolation. I've flagged the appropriate cells in the Ops Impact tab.

Karthik
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Priya Menon <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T14:27:00-04:00
Subject: Re: SCCs: decision matrix + local law considerations for Acme Health

Thanks, Aisha and Karthik — helpful matrix. A few clarifications from Acme legal / DPO side: 

1) UK Addendum: Our UK counsel asked whether the addendum text references the UK implementation of the adequacy regime (we prefer explicit mention of the UK Addendum clause and the fallback to the EU SCCs where applicable). Can Redwood confirm you will accept the combined EU SCCs + UK Addendum execution in a single signature flow?

2) Audit rights: We do require the ability to request audit evidence for inpatient treatment logs (sampled quarterly). Please confirm how Redwood will surface those logs and whether we can have read-only access to specific event traces (redacted for Redwood internal IDs).

3) Local law note — security: Given the health context, will Redwood commit to route all PHI-adjacent processing through EU/UK-only capacity by default? If not, we need a strong fallback justification and documented mitigation (e.g., encrypted processing, customer-held keys).

If you can confirm the options for 1) combined execution flow, 2) audit evidence access, and 3) processing region defaults, we can move to a short legal redline.

Best,
Priya
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Priya Menon <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SCCs: decision matrix + local law considerations for Acme Health

Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Summary / decisions we can commit to now: 

1) Combined EU SCCs + UK Addendum execution: Yes — Redwood accepts executing the EU SCCs with the UK Addendum as a single contract flow. We'll provide a signing package that includes both documents and a cover sheet stating the applicability (EU + UK).

2) Audit evidence: We can provide quarterly sampled audit exports for inpatient treatment logs. Format: CSV export of event traces with Redwood-internal identifiers redacted; includes timestamps, processed fields, and retention markers. We will provide a read-only S3 share or secure transfer link for evidence delivery. We'll add the delivery SLA (10 business days from request) into the evidence appendix.

3) Processing region defaults: We will route PHI-adjacent processing to EU/UK-only capacity by default. Any temporary routing outside EU/UK will require written approval from Acme and be limited in scope; such events will be captured in a routing log that Acme can request. For customers who insist on customer-held keys, we can surface a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option but it requires an ops onboarding (~3 weeks).

Next steps / action items: 
- Redwood legal will incorporate these commitments into the contract redline and return a draft by EOD Friday (redline link: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/legal/SCCs/Acme-Redline).
- Ops (Karthik) to prepare the evidence export prototype and sample CSV schema; aim for demo next week.
- Acme to confirm whether quarterly sampling is acceptable or if they require continuous audit stream for a subset of events.

I'll loop Jonas for executive visibility on the service-level commitment. Thanks — we can move to signatures once legal redlines are exchanged.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: sccs-decision-matrix.xlsx (updated), uk-addendum-draft.pdf (annotated)
